**Solution 3 is correct; the area is 200.**

Place the external homothety center H at the origin with the line of centers as the x-axis. The tangents are ℓ₁, ℓ₂ through H at angles ±θ. Since PQ is perpendicular to the line of centers, P = (c, 5) and Q = (c, −5).

The distances from P to the tangents give |5cosθ − c sinθ| = 3 and |5cosθ + c sinθ| = 12. The only solution with |5cosθ| ≤ 5 is cosθ = 0.9, c sinθ = 7.5, so sin θ = √19/10 and c = 75/√19.

A circle centered at (a, 0) with radius a sinθ passes through P when 0.81a² − 2ca + (c² + 25) = 0. The roots a₁, a₂ are both positive, with
- a₁ + a₂ = 2c/0.81 = 150/(0.81√19),
- |a₂ − a₁| = √(4(0.19c² − 20.25)/0.6561) = 12/0.81, using 0.19c² = 56.25.

The tangency points are U₁, U₂ = (a₁cos²θ, ±a₁cosθ sinθ) and V₁, V₂ = (a₂cos²θ, ±a₂cosθ sinθ). So U₁U₂V₂V₁ is a trapezoid with vertical parallel sides of lengths 2a₁cosθ sinθ and 2a₂cosθ sinθ, separated horizontally by |a₂ − a₁|cos²θ. Its area is

Area = cosθ sinθ · cos²θ · (a₁ + a₂) · |a₂ − a₁|
= (0.09√19)(0.81)(150/(0.81√19))(12/0.81)
= 0.09 · 1800 / 0.81 = 200.

Solution 1 wrongly assumes the tangents are parallel, which contradicts PQ = 10. Solution 2's value 16√19 ≈ 69.8 does not match this computation.

CHOICE: 3
